documentation.range: Choloepus didactylus ranges through Venezuela (the delta and south of the Río Orinoco) and the Guianas (French Guiana, Guyana, and Suriname) south into Brazil (Maranhão state west along the Rio Amazonas/Solimões) and west into the upper Amazon Basin of Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia. Additional visual records from southeastern Pará State, Brazil, need to be confirmed. Its southern limit in the western Amazon of Brazil is unclear. It occurs in the southern departments of Colombia, with its northern limit being the departments of Meta and Guainía. It ranges from sea level up to 2,400 m asl (Britton 1941).
documentation.population:
In French Guiana, C. didactylus has been found at densities of 0.9 animals per hectare (Taube et al. 1999). In the Brazilian Amazon, estimated densities range from 0.13 individuals per hectare (Manaus region) to 0.88 animals per hectare in the flooded forests (Mamirauá Reserve; Queiroz 1995, Chiarello 2008).

There is evidence suggesting a differentiation between western and eastern populations; the diploid numbers range between 2n = 52–54 and 2n = 64–65 (Moraes-Barros 2018). A taxonomic reevaluation is needed to ensure the proper conservation of the species.
documentation.habitats:
Choloepus didactylus is found in tropical moist lowland and montane forest. In Suriname and French Guiana it does not occur in mangroves. Two-toed sloths have nocturnal and solitary habits. Gestation length seems to be approximately 10 months (Eisenberg and Maliniak 1985) but estimates are quite variable.

There is little information on the diet of wild individuals (Chiarello 2008). A rather unusual observation in the Amazon of north-eastern Peru recorded an adult individual descending to the forest floor to feed on a human latrine (Heymann et al. 2011).
documentation.threats:
The species is affected by habitat loss due to deforestation for large-scale agriculture, logging, exploration for mining and other activities, and urban sprawl (especially in Suriname). In Brazil, habitat loss within the species' extent of occurrence (EOO) as a result of the increase of pasturelands and soybean crops has been estimated at 9.4% (P.M. Santos pers. comm. 2022).

It is also affected by wildfires, which can kill the animals or affect them indirectly through habitat loss. The species is illegally sold as a pet species in several parts of this range, but the impact of this activity is difficult to quantify.

Because they are usually found high in the canopy, motionless and virtually invisible, they are not as commonly hunted as armadillos or anteaters, and there are taboos against their consumption by some native groups. They are probably hunted opportunistically, but there is no serious bushmeat trade.
documentation.measures: Choloepus didactylus is present in many protected areas.
documentation.use_trade: Choloepus didactylus is probably hunted opportunistically, but there is no serious bushmeat trade. The illegal trafficking of the species seems to be increasing in Bolivia, where Choloepus didactylus is captured and sold as a pet. Although it is illegal to keep wildlife as pets (Presidencia del Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia 2021), this practice seems to be increasing.
documentation.rationale: Choloepus didactylus is listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, presumed large population and its occurrence in a number of protected areas. The species is affected by several threats, especially habitat loss due to wildfires and land use change. However, it is unlikely to be declining fast enough to qualify for listing in a threatened category.
